Upload a file, then send a chat message with its id: PDFs and text files are read into the agent's prompt, images go to the model as multimodal input. The default limit is 10 MB per file.
The agent receives the extracted PDF text before the user message. The reply streams to WebSocket clients (see Gateway Chat).

Content type Processing What the agent sees application/pdf Text extracted with pypdf (a dependency of aiui) --- Attached PDF: name --- block before the message image/* File path passed to the agent's attachments The image, for vision-capable models Anything else allowed File read as text --- Attached File: name --- block before the message

POST /api/chat/attachments accepts three encodings so uploads work out of the box even without python-multipart: Raw binary body with X-Filename header and file Content-Type (what aiui.file_upload() sends). JSON body ({"filename", "content_type", "data_base64", "session_id?"}). multipart/form-data with a file field (when python-multipart is installed; returns HTTP 415 otherwise). Category MIME types Text & Markup text/plain, text/csv, text/tab-separated-values, text/markdown (text/x-markdown normalized), application/xml, text/xml Data & Office application/json, application/pdf, .xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), .docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document) Images image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, image/webp Audio audio/mpeg, audio/wav, audio/webm, audio/ogg, audio/mp4 Common OS MIME quirks (such as Windows sending application/vnd.ms-excel for .csv, or application/octet-stream for known safe data/media extensions) are normalized safely. Active web types (text/html, image/svg+xml, application/javascript) are always rejected with 400 {"error": "Type not allowed: ..."}. Files over the size limit return 413 / 400. Files are stored under /praisonai_attachments/ with sanitized UUID filenames, automatic TTL eviction (default 3600 seconds) and capacity eviction (default 500 entries). Internal filesystem path values are never returned in HTTP responses — resolve them server-side with aiui.get_uploaded_file().

On @aiui.page and aiui.interface() forms, use aiui.file_upload() to render a drag-and-drop uploader and resolve the uploaded handle safely in Python: Inside a manual @aiui.register_page_action handler, always resolve client handles via meta = aiui.get_uploaded_file(data.get("doc")) — it validates UUID syntax and looks up the file in the server's registry, blocking path traversal and expired/forged handles.
Add -F "index_to_knowledge=true" to the upload to also store the file in the knowledge base. The response then carries knowledge_indexed (and knowledge_error when it failed).

AttachmentManager(storage_dir=None, max_size_mb=10, allowed_types=None) takes the limits. The server creates its default instance with praisonaiui.features.attachments.get_attachment_manager(); there is no public setter for a custom one yet.

Endpoint Method Description /api/chat/attachments POST Upload a file (multipart: file, optional session_id, index_to_knowledge) /api/chat/attachments/{session_id} GET List a session's attachments /api/chat/attachments/{attachment_id} DELETE Delete an attachment /api/chat/media/{attachment_id} GET Serve a stored generated-media file
Over the WebSocket, put attachment_ids in the chat frame: POST /run (the chat's HTTP fallback when the WebSocket cannot open) takes the same attachment_ids and handles them the same way.
Text and PDF files are put before the message text. Every file of the message is also on message.attachments, so an app can read images itself:
Gateway Chat: the chat interface Sessions: session management
